source_citation: Manta et al. (2023), Predicting the Loop Current dynamics combining altimetry and deep flow measurements through the Yucatan Channel, Frontiers in Marine Science 10:1156159, doi:10.3389/fmars.2023.1156159.
source_access: Full publisher HTML methods and results read. Figures were not digitized. Supplemental numerical Loop Current paths were not acquired.
source_product: Copernicus DUACS DT-2018 daily 0.25-degree absolute dynamic topography and surface geostrophic velocity

published_metrics.method: Demeaned 0.17 m sea-level contour connecting Yucatan Channel and Florida Straits
Maximum-geostrophic-velocity streamline connecting Yucatan Channel and Florida Straits

range_interpretation: Source describes retracted states below 1000 km and extended phases around 1800–2600 km. These are phase descriptions, not an annual extrema range, confidence interval or width.
comparison_result: Highest length-weighted mean speed among 31 eligible gateway-connected ADT contours occurs at 0.62 m ADT. Selected path rounds to 2200 km and is 55.9 km shorter than the NOAA trace before display rounding. This is product/method disagreement, not independent observation, uncertainty or a physical range.
diagnostic_method: OSW frozen-time velocity integration with strongest northward native-grid seed at an editorial regional gate; distinct from both source contour algorithms
diagnostic_source_product: NOAA LSA RADS 4.8.1 Experimental daily absolute surface geostrophic velocities; lacks absolute dynamic topography
diagnostic_result: Nominal gateway-connected path rounds to 2300 km; all four neighboring seed scenarios fail. Integration step changes are small, but no robust range follows from only successful tests.
remaining_gates: Validate gateway placement and section alternatives using geographic and bathymetric evidence
Compatible same-date DUACS ADT acquired through GCOOS; recover original supplemental maximum-velocity algorithm and compare its gateway/method choices
Preserve failed seed outcomes and assess effective resolution and grid masks
Four predeclared dates tested; assess original method/gateway choices and broader repeated-date coverage before describing physical variability or seasonal ranges
Complete scientific and regional raw-subset source-use review before admission/publication
recorded_date_result: Predeclared 15 January, April, July and October 2025 snapshots: NOAA connects only on April 15 (1573.2 km), failing at missing velocity on three dates. DUACS selects contours on all four dates (2082.9, 1592.7, 1674.0, 989.4 km); April difference 19.5 km. Four recorded days are not annual extrema, phase labels or a climatology. Preserve product/method failures.
